subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Birth of John the Baptist
overview: John the Baptist was born to Zechariah and Elizabeth after an angel spoke in the temple. In this sub-strand you will retell Luke 1:5-13 and 57, then read Luke 1:76-79 to see how John would prepare the way for the Messiah. You will also learn why a righteous life means turning away from sin.

lessons.title: The promise and the birth
objectives: Retell the birth of John the Baptist from Luke 1:5-13 and 57.
Describe the angel's appearance to Zechariah.
lessons.intro: Some families wait many years for a child. Zechariah and Elizabeth had waited. While Zechariah was serving in the temple, an angel told him that their prayer had been heard.
lessons.notes:
Read Luke 1:5-13 and verse 57 in pairs. Retell only those verses.

### Zechariah and Elizabeth
In the time of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah. He belonged to the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was Elizabeth. She also came from the family of Aaron, the priestly family. Both of them were righteous in God's sight. They obeyed the Lord's commands and were blameless. They had no child, because Elizabeth was not able to conceive, and they were both very old.

### The angel in the temple
When Zechariah's division was on duty, he was chosen by lot to go into the temple of the Lord and burn incense. The worshippers were praying outside. An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. Zechariah was startled and gripped with fear.

The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to call him John."

### The birth
Luke 1:57 says that when it was time for Elizabeth to have her baby, she gave birth to a son. The verses you are reading do not describe the naming ceremony. You already know from verse 13 that the angel said the child was to be called John.

Role-play the temple scene: Zechariah at the altar, the people praying outside, and the angel at the right side of the altar. Keep the fear, the comfort "Do not be afraid," and the promise of a son named John.

keyWords.meaning: a person set apart to serve God in the temple, as Zechariah did
a spice burned in worship, which Zechariah was chosen to burn
living in a way that is right before God

activity.title: Role-play the angel in the temple
steps: Role-play the angel's appearance to Zechariah in the temple.
Retell the story from the couple's righteousness to the birth of the son.
If a video clip on the birth of John the Baptist is available, watch it and check it against the verses.

practice.question: Who were John's parents, and why did they have no child?
practice.answer: Zechariah and Elizabeth. They had no child because Elizabeth was not able to conceive, and they were both very old.

practice.question: Where did the angel stand, and what did he tell Zechariah?
practice.answer: At the right side of the altar of incense. He said their prayer had been heard, Elizabeth would bear a son, and the son was to be called John.

practice.question: What does Luke 1:57 say happened?
practice.answer: Elizabeth gave birth to a son.

summary: Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous, old, and childless.
An angel told Zechariah in the temple that they would have a son named John.
Elizabeth gave birth to a son.

lessons.title: Preparing the way and turning from sin
objectives: Explain from Luke 1:76-79 how John prepared the way for the Messiah.
Appreciate the need to live a righteous life by turning away from sin.
lessons.intro: A precursor goes ahead to prepare people for someone greater. Luke 1:76-79 says John would go before the Lord to prepare His way. That Lord is the Messiah, Jesus Christ.
lessons.notes:
After John was born, his father Zechariah spoke about him. Luke 1:76-79 is the part we read. It says:

- The child would be called a prophet of the Most High.
- He would go before the Lord to prepare the way for Him.
- He would give God's people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.
- This would happen because of the tender mercy of God.
- The rising sun would come from heaven to shine on those living in darkness and in the shadow of death.
- He would guide their feet into the path of peace.

### How John prepared the way
He did not come to take the Lord's place. He went before the Lord. He was a prophet who pointed people to salvation and to the forgiveness of sins. He was to lead people out of darkness into the path of peace. In that way he prepared people for the Messiah. The key question asks how John is a precursor of Jesus Christ. A precursor is someone who goes ahead. Verse 76 says John would go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him.

### A righteous life
Luke 1:6 says Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous and obeyed God's commands. Verse 77 speaks of forgiveness of sins. A righteous life is not pretending to be perfect. It is turning away from sins and walking in God's commands.

You turn away from sin when you:

- Stop a wrong action, such as lying or stealing.
- Ask God for forgiveness.
- Choose the path of peace instead of quarrels.
- Obey at home and at school.

Appreciate this need. Do not admire sin. Thank God for His tender mercy, and sing a song about John the Baptist, the prophet who prepared the way.

keyWords.meaning: the Lord and Saviour whom John prepared people to receive
someone who goes ahead to prepare the way
a person who speaks God's message, as John was called a prophet of the Most High

activity.title: Read Luke 1:76-79
steps: Tell how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah, using the verses.
List sins a learner should turn away from, and the right action that replaces each one.
Sing a song about John the Baptist.

practice.question: What would John be called, and what would he do before the Lord?
practice.answer: A prophet of the Most High. He would go before the Lord to prepare the way for Him.

practice.question: Through what would people know salvation, according to Luke 1:77?
practice.answer: Through the forgiveness of their sins.

practice.question: What does it mean to live a righteous life?
practice.answer: To turn away from sin and obey God's commands.

summary: John would go before the Lord as a prophet to prepare His way.
He would point people to salvation through the forgiveness of sins.
A righteous life means turning away from sin.

quiz.question: John's parents were...
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:5 names Zechariah the priest and his wife Elizabeth.

quiz.question: Why were they childless?
options: Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and they were very old

quiz.question: The angel stood...
options: at the right side of the altar of incense
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:11 places the angel at the right side of the altar of incense.

quiz.question: The child was to be called...
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:13 says, "You are to call him John."

quiz.question: Luke 1:57 says Elizabeth...
quiz.explanation: That is the birth verse set for this sub-strand.

quiz.question: John prepared the way for the Messiah by...
options: going before the Lord and pointing people to forgiveness
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:76-77 says he would go before the Lord and give knowledge of salvation through forgiveness of sins.

quiz.question: A precursor is someone who...
options: goes ahead to prepare the way
quiz.explanation: John is a precursor because he went before the Lord.

quiz.question: Luke 1:79 says John would guide people's feet into...
quiz.explanation: The verse says he would guide their feet into the path of peace.

quiz.question: Zechariah and Elizabeth are called righteous because...
options: they never served in the temple
quiz.explanation: Luke 1:6 says they observed all the Lord's commands blamelessly.

quiz.question: Living a righteous life means...
quiz.answer: Turning away from sin and obeying God.
quiz.explanation: Forgiveness and obedience belong together in this lesson.
